Bhutan Imposes Temporary Export Restrictions on Electricity; Utilities Grapple With Uncertainty

The Royal Government of Bhutan has imposed temporary restrictions on electricity exports in response to prolonged drought conditions, affecting the Electric Utilities industry nationwide. The measure, announced last week, requires utilities to prioritize domestic supply over cross-border sales, resulting in immediate operational and financial repercussions.

Leading power producers such as Druk Green Power Corp Ltd and Bhutan Hydel Energy Services are now operating under revised export quotas. Industry sources indicate that export volumes to neighboring countries have dropped by as much as 45% since implementation. Bhutan’s state-owned utilities had relied on cross-border sales to India as a major revenue source, and this sudden policy shift is straining cash flows.

“We understand the government’s concern for national energy security, but this restriction is already impacting our contractual obligations and revenue projections,” said Sonam Dorji, spokesperson for Druk Green Power Corp Ltd. The company is reportedly renegotiating delivery schedules with regional partners but warns of potential delays in project expansion plans.

Analysts note the move was prompted by record-low water levels in Bhutan’s river systems, which have slashed hydropower generation capacity. “The decision was inevitable given the climatic challenges,” said Karma Wangchuk, a trade policy analyst based in Thimphu. “But the utilities sector faces tough months ahead as it adapts to rapidly changing supply dynamics.”

The Bhutan Electricity Association has called for government consultation and support to help utilities manage the financial fallout. “We urge policymakers to work closely with the industry to mitigate losses and secure the sector’s long-term viability,” said the association in a statement.

The export restrictions remain in effect, with officials indicating they will be reviewed as hydrological conditions evolve.
